title: Test & quality system — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: Softanza has no test framework as a module — it has a test-and-quality discipline spread across the estate, and its signature is that a test is a readable specification and a green checkmark is never enough. 455 narrated guards read as Given/When/Then specs; correctness is proven against independent numpy/LAPACK oracles (not just self-captured snapshots), by byte-parity against pre-port ground truth, and by an adversarial gate whose 1,416 assertions each exist because "a defect survived a green suite" — with 58 negative controls that prove the instrument itself can fail. Distribution is tested on real spawned processes; the engine is fuzzed and property-tested; and one rule gate collects code, security, agent and diagram findings in a single shape. Where it's thin: property/mutation is engine-only, there is no coverage instrumentation and no CI, and the classic suites carry a fidelity backlog.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: A cross-cutting system measured against the basket most projects assemble from separate tools — pytest/jest, Hypothesis, libFuzzer, jest-snapshot, Cucumber, SonarQube. The split is clean: the techniques are rigorous; the tooling (coverage, CI, the classic-suite backlog) lags.

lanes.engine: `_narrated.ring` gives a Given/When/Then DSL (`Scenario` / `Then(text, got, want)` / `Summary`) that prints a readable spec and distinguishes "ran-but-failed" from "didn't run" — across 455 `*_narrated.ring` guards and on the order of 10,000+ assertions.
lanes.owed: BDD-as-default at estate scale. The one wart: the dominant per-file `chk(label, cond)` idiom is copy-pasted, not imported — a convention rather than one shipped assertion module (lane 12).

lanes.engine: Correctness checked against an independent implementation, not self-consistency: `_gen_numpy_reference.py` generates `_numpy_reference.ring` / `_numpy_fft_reference.ring` (LAPACK eigenvalues, SVD, det, Cholesky…), and the BERT forward matches numpy to 1.64e-7.
lanes.owed: Oracle testing catches bugs a snapshot cannot — a snapshot pins whatever you produced, right or wrong; an oracle pins what is correct. A gold-standard technique used where it matters most (numeric, neural).

lanes.engine: `gg_adversarial.ring` (23,481 lines, 1,416 assertions): its thesis is "every assertion exists because a defect survived a green suite and was found by rendering a picture and looking at it." It carries 58 negative siblings (proving each instrument can fail) and 82 `discharges()` that generate the plan's status table from the suite.
lanes.owed: Assertions born from real escaped defects, negative controls, and a plan-discharge link — a rigor discipline most suites never reach. Distinctive.

lanes.engine: `stzRuleReport` collects findings in one shape `[:rule,:subject,:where,:severity,:message]` from 13 rule domains (code, security, agent, org, service, and diagram notations), with `IsSound()`; 14 code rules + the knob gate; and a signable predicate set (`stzPredicateSet`, sha256-sealed `.zrlz`).
lanes.owed: One gate over code and security and agent and process rules — a unification SonarQube/semgrep (code-only) don't attempt (rated deeper on the Metaprogramming page). Its one weakness: it isn't wired to any CI (lane 12).

lanes.engine: `plot.zig` holds 29 byte-parity tests against ground truth captured from the Ring plotters before the renderer moved (and after three defects were fixed); `stzLLMFunction.AddGolden/RunGoldens` pins LLM outputs; and the `#-->` markers capture expected stdout.
lanes.owed: Rigorous snapshot testing (captured post-fix, string-exact) — but snapshots pin current behavior, so a wrong-but-stable output can be frozen; the oracle lane (2) is the stronger guard where it applies.

lanes.engine: Five UBSan-trap fuzzers on the untrusted-input parsers — `fuzz_http`, `fuzz_tls` (X.509), `fuzz_pcre2` (300k rounds, ReDoS-bounded), `fuzz_sqlite`, `fuzz_utf8` — wired into `zig build fuzz`, any UB becoming a hard crash.
lanes.owed: Real fuzzing of exactly the right targets — but engine-only (5 harnesses), random-round not coverage-guided (no libFuzzer feedback or evolving corpus), and not run continuously.

lanes.engine: The D0–D6 cluster guards spawn genuine OS processes (via `uv_spawn`), exchange framed STZM messages over loopback, perform real kills to test supervision, and assert clean teardown; the appserver guards run a second reactor as a live client.
lanes.owed: Integration testing against real processes and real failures (not mocks) — rigorous where it exists, but a focused set (cluster / appserver), not a general integration-test framework.

lanes.engine: Inline `test "…"` blocks in 151 of 371 engine `.zig` files — the native Zig unit layer under the Ring guards, run by the build's test step.
lanes.owed: Standard, well-used inline unit testing at the engine layer. Coverage of the 371-file engine is broad but not universal (151 files), and unmeasured (lane 12).

lanes.engine: Million-scale guards (1M-item `IntSeq` builds ~7 ms vs >60 s; `999_*_millions` string/list suites) and multilingual stress (Arabic/CJK/emoji through the same paths), catching O(n²) regressions and byte-corruption at scale.
lanes.owed: Scale and multilingual correctness are tested as first-class properties — a real strength — though the timed guards inherit the machine-load sensitivity the perf plane documents.

lanes.engine: The narrated guards are designed to double as readable specs, and a parallel prose corpus of 135 narrations (`base/doc/narrations`) explains the same features the guards prove — a runnable-and-readable pairing.
lanes.owed: A genuine test-as-doc intent — but the guard↔narration link is convention, not enforced: the two can (and once did) diverge, letting a bug hide behind a prettied-up narration.

lanes.engine: Three `prop_*.zig` files — `prop_crypto` (determinism / tamper-detection plus mutation: "constant + first-byte hashes must be killed"), `prop_http`, `prop_ratebucket` (token-bucket invariants).
lanes.owed: Engine-only, 3 files. No Ring-side property testing, no generator/shrinking framework (Hypothesis), and no mutation-testing framework for the library — the mutation discipline lives only inside those crypto/http/ratebucket props.

lanes.engine: Coverage is by assertion count (chk / Then / `#-->` / discharged plan items); the pipeline is bespoke Python runners (`_run_test_batch.py`, `_annotate_test_errors.py`, `promises.py`) plus `zig build`.
lanes.owed: No coverage % (no line/branch instrumentation), no CI config (`.github` absent), and a fidelity-grind backlog: the classic `#-->` suites sit ~41–60% green with 1,312 `#ERR` markers, while the curated narrated surface is the green, maintained one.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The techniques are strong; the gaps are tooling and hygiene — the first tier makes the discipline enforceable, the second broadens it, the third pays down debt.

tiers.title: Tier A — make the discipline enforceable

items.title: A standard CI pipeline
items.text: There is no `.github` / CI config — the bespoke runners and `zig build` should run on every push, with the unified rule gate (`stzRuleReport`) as a required check. The whole point of a quality gate is to gate; today it's a library API nothing runs automatically.

items.title: Coverage instrumentation
items.text: Line/branch coverage for the engine (and, where feasible, the Ring guards) so "we assert a lot" becomes "we cover X%." Assertion counts show effort, not reach — the one number this rigorous system cannot currently produce.

items.title: Ring-side property testing
items.text: A Hypothesis-style generator/shrinking harness for Ring library code — property testing is engine-only (3 files) today. It would fit the library's "assert the mechanism" ethos and find the edge cases example-based guards miss.

items.title: A shipped assertion module
items.text: Retire the copy-pasted per-file `chk()` for one imported harness (the `_narrated.ring` DSL is the seed), so every guard shares one tallying, diffing, skip-aware assertion surface instead of 455 near-copies.

items.title: Coverage-guided / continuous fuzzing
items.text: Give the five fuzzers libFuzzer-style coverage feedback and an evolving corpus, and run them continuously in CI — turning random-round harnesses into corpus-growing regression fuzzers.

tiers.title: Tier C — pay down the debt

items.title: Close the fidelity-grind backlog
items.text: The classic `#-->` suites sit ~41–60% green with 1,312 `#ERR` — mostly output drift and lost shared setup, not real bugs. Reconciling them makes the whole corpus vouch, not just the curated narrated surface.

items.title: Mutation testing for Ring code
items.text: Extend the engine's "these mutations must be killed" discipline (today only in the crypto/http/ratebucket props) into a mutation-testing pass over the library — the strongest measure of whether the many assertions actually catch defects.

items.title: Enforce the guard↔narration link
items.text: Bind each prose narration to the guard that proves it, so the two can't diverge silently (the underscore-vs-space case where a bug hid behind a prettified narration) — turning test-as-doc from convention into contract.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: This page rates a cross-cutting system, not a module — there is no `base/test-framework`; it is ~6 harnesses/gates plus a large guard corpus. Read from `main`. The strengths are technique-level and real (455 narrated guards; `plot.zig` byte-parity; numpy/LAPACK oracles; `gg_adversarial`'s 1,416 assertions + 58 negative controls + 82 plan-discharges; D0–D6 real-process; 5 engine fuzzers + 3 property/mutation files; the 13-domain rule gate). The weaknesses are tooling-level and honestly recorded in the repo's own health files (`base/test/_STATUS.md` / `_FINDINGS.md`): no coverage %, no CI, and the classic-suite backlog. The split is the story: the curated narrated / adversarial / oracle surface is green and maintained; the classic extracted suites are the grind.

Softanza tests the way it builds — narrated as a spec, proven against independent oracles and negative controls, gated in one place — a testing discipline more rigorous than most frameworks demand; what it lacks is the ordinary tooling those frameworks ship for free: coverage numbers, a CI that runs the gate, and a reconciled classic-suite corpus.

footer: Read from the source on 2026-09-17, from a read-only `main` worktree — the narrated-guard harness `base/test/_narrated.ring` (455 `*_narrated.ring` guards); the promise harness `base/meta/promises.py` (~8,500 `#-->` markers) with runners `_run_test_batch.py` / `_annotate_test_errors.py`; engine `test` blocks (151/371 files), fuzzers `fuzz_{http,tls,pcre2,sqlite,utf8}.zig` and `prop_{crypto,http,ratebucket}.zig`; oracles `_gen_numpy_reference.py`, byte-parity in `plot.zig`, the gate `base/graph/stzRuleReport.ring` + `stzPredicateSet`; health in `base/test/_STATUS.md` / `_FINDINGS.md`. Ratings reflect what the guards prove.
